anchors.description: Straight-line distance from the front bottom rail of the upper wall cabinet (above the right-hand counter) to the countertop surface at the backsplash base directly below it; the standard counter-to-upper-cabinet backsplash gap is 18 in, and the endpoints are also offset by about the cabinet depth (front rail stands ~12 in out from the wall).
anchors.visible_evidence: Orange-wood upper cabinet bottom rail is visible above the white tiled backsplash (p23 sits on that rail at y~110); the white counter plane carrying the blue board and dishpan is visible at y~164, with p13 at the blue board's lower-left corner on the counter. The rail is at the cabinet front face, p13 near the wall plane.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: The counter-to-upper-cabinet gap is commonly 18 in but ranges 15-24 in by installation; the two points are additionally offset along the wall (a few inches) and in depth (cabinet front vs backsplash plane), so the 3D chord exceeds the pure vertical gap; the interval budgets both effects.
